bibleSpine.kjv: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
bibleSpine.gloss: The core justification text: righteousness is a free gift of grace received through faith in Christ's blood, wholly apart from the deeds of the law, so that God is at once JUST (the law upheld) and the JUSTIFIER of the believer. Boasting is excluded — the ground is faith, not works.

bibleSpine.kjv: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.
bibleSpine.gloss: Righteousness is COUNTED (imputed/reckoned), not earned. The one who works is paid a debt; the one who works not but believes on the God who justifies the ungodly has his faith counted for righteousness. This is the title, credited freely.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
bibleSpine.gloss: The original of Paul's argument: Abraham's faith counted for righteousness. Justification by faith is not a New Testament innovation but the gospel preached from the beginning.

bibleSpine.kjv: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.
bibleSpine.gloss: The imputation to Abraham is written 'for us also' — the same righteousness is reckoned to every believer. Christ was delivered for our offences and raised for our justification: the risen Christ is the ground of the imputed title.

bibleSpine.kjv: In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Messiah's own name is THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS. Our righteousness is not a quality we manufacture but a Person we receive — Christ Himself, credited and indwelling.

bibleSpine.kjv: But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ is MADE UNTO US righteousness (the imputed title) AND sanctification (the imparted fitness) — the same Christ supplies both. There is no righteousness apart from being in Him.

bibleSpine.kjv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
bibleSpine.gloss: The gospel reveals 'the righteousness of God' — not man's, but God's own — received 'from faith to faith.' The banner text of the Reformation and of 1888: THE JUST SHALL LIVE BY FAITH.

bibleSpine.kjv: Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Old Testament root of Paul's thesis. The proud, self-lifted soul is not upright; the just man lives — from justification onward — by faith, not by his own works.

bibleSpine.kjv: But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:
bibleSpine.gloss: The righteousness of God, apart from law-keeping as its source, is 'by faith of Jesus Christ' and comes 'upon all them that believe' — the imputed robe placed upon the believer without distinction of persons.

bibleSpine.kjv: And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith:
bibleSpine.gloss: Paul renounces his own law-righteousness to be 'found in Him' clothed with 'the righteousness which is of God by faith.' The believer's standing is a borrowed, God-given righteousness, never a self-produced one.

bibleSpine.kjv: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
bibleSpine.gloss: The great exchange: the sinless One was made sin, that we might be MADE the righteousness of God in Him. This is imputation stated in its sharpest form — His righteousness for our sin.

bibleSpine.kjv: For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.
bibleSpine.gloss: The faith that justifies is never a dead assent: it is 'faith which worketh by love.' Imparted righteousness is the living activity of the same faith that receives the imputed title. Obedience is faith's fruit.

bibleSpine.kjv: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
bibleSpine.gloss: The formula of imparted righteousness: 'not I, but Christ liveth in me.' The believer's new life is Christ's own life lived by faith within him — Christ's obedience wrought in fallen man, not merely credited to him.

bibleSpine.kjv: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
bibleSpine.gloss: God's purpose is not only imputed but imparted: the righteousness of the law is 'fulfilled IN us' by Christ, who came in the likeness of sinful flesh and condemned sin there. Righteousness by faith produces real obedience — never optional.

bibleSpine.kjv: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
bibleSpine.gloss: Salvation is the gift of God through faith, not of works — yet the saved are His workmanship, created unto good works. Works are excluded as the ROOT of salvation and required as its FRUIT: the balance the section owns.

bibleSpine.kjv: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
bibleSpine.gloss: The immediate fruit of justification by faith is peace with God through Christ — the settled standing of the believer whose title rests on Another's righteousness.

bibleSpine.kjv: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone. Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.
bibleSpine.gloss: The needed guard against a false, workless 'faith': faith without works is dead. Genuine justifying faith proves itself in works — obedience is the visible evidence of the living faith that saves, never its purchase price.

symbolDefs.meaning: Christ's own righteousness given to the believer in two inseparable modes: IMPUTED — His obedience credited/counted/reckoned to the one who believes, so that God, remaining just, justifies the ungodly (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 3:24-28; 4:3-5, 22-25; 2 Cor. 5:21; Phil. 3:9) — this is the believer's TITLE to heaven; and IMPARTED — the same Christ living in the believer by faith, fulfilling the righteousness of the law in him, so the faith works by love (Rom. 8:3-4; Gal. 2:20; Gal. 5:6; 1 Cor. 1:30) — this is the believer's FITNESS. It is 'the righteousness of God' (Rom. 1:17; 3:21-22), not man's; its very Name is THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS (Jer. 23:6). Obedience is its fruit, never its root, and never optional (Eph. 2:8-10; Jas. 2:17-18).

symbolDefs.symbol: the just shall live by faith
symbolDefs.meaning: The believer enters righteousness by faith and continues the entire Christian life by that same faith — total dependence on the word of God. The just man is first counted just by faith (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3-5) and then lives, day by day, by precisely the same principle by which he became just: not law-works, but reliance on Christ (Hab. 2:4; Rom. 1:17). Self-lifted, self-sufficient works are excluded.

To credit to the believer's account a righteousness he did not earn. Abraham 'believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness'; to him that worketh not but believeth, 'his faith is counted for righteousness'; it was written 'for us also, to whom it shall be imputed.' God 'made him to be sin for us... that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.' This is the legal ground of the believer's title.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Several have written to me, inquiring if the message of justification by faith is the third angel's message, and I have answered, "It is the third angel's message, in verity."
witnesses.gloss: The definitive statement that the 1888 message of justification by faith IS the third angel's message in verity — the confirming witness that anchors this entire section's thesis. Originally The Review and Herald, April 1, 1890.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Some of our brethren have expressed fears that we shall dwell too much upon the subject of justification by faith, but I hope and pray that none will be needlessly alarmed; for there is no danger in presenting this doctrine as it is set forth in the Scriptures. If there had not been a remissness in the past to properly instruct the people of God, there would not now be a necessity of calling a special attention to it.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms that righteousness by faith is to be preached fully and fearlessly as set forth in Scripture — not a softer standard but the neglected heart of the message.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The proud heart strives to earn salvation; but both our title to heaven and our fitness for it are found in the righteousness of Christ.
witnesses.gloss: The exact imputed/imparted frame of the section: TITLE (imputed) and FITNESS (imparted) are BOTH found in Christ's righteousness, never self-earned. Confirms 1 Cor. 1:30 and Phil. 3:9.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The grace of Christ is freely to justify the sinner without merit or claim on his part. Justification is a full, complete pardon of sin. The moment a sinner accepts Christ by faith, that moment he is pardoned. The righteousness of Christ is imputed to him, and he is no more to doubt God's forgiving grace.
witnesses.gloss: Defines justification as full pardon and confirms the imputed righteousness of Christ received freely by faith 'without merit or claim' — a direct confirmation of Rom. 3:24-28 and 4:3-5.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Pardon and justification are one and the same thing. Through faith, the believer passes from the position of a rebel, a child of sin and Satan, to the position of a loyal subject of Christ Jesus, not because of an inherent goodness, but because Christ receives him as His child by adoption.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms that justification is God's act of pardon received through faith, resting on Christ and not on inherent goodness — the imputed title of Rom. 5:1.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The incense, ascending with the prayers of Israel, represents the merits and intercession of Christ, His perfect righteousness, which through faith is imputed to His people, and which can alone make the worship of sinful beings acceptable to God.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the imputed righteousness of Christ through faith as the sole ground on which sinful worship is accepted — the sanctuary picture of Rom. 3:22 and 2 Cor. 5:21.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: John did not teach that salvation was to be earned by obedience; but that obedience was the fruit of faith and love... If we abide in Christ, if the love of God dwells in the heart, our feelings, our thoughts, our actions, will be in harmony with the will of God. The sanctified heart is in harmony with the precepts of God's law.
witnesses.gloss: The section's exact balance: obedience is the FRUIT of faith, not the means of earning salvation — yet the sanctified heart truly harmonizes with God's law. Confirms Gal. 5:6, Rom. 8:4, and Eph. 2:8-10.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Righteousness is right doing, and it is by their deeds that all will be judged. Our characters are revealed by what we do. The works show whether the faith is genuine.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms that genuine justifying faith is never workless: works reveal whether faith is real — the guard of Jas. 2:17-18 that obedience is faith's necessary evidence.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: At last the sinner, weary of the vain struggle to get righteousness from the law, listens to the voice of Christ and flees to His outstretched arms. Hiding in Christ, he is covered with His righteousness, and now behold! he has obtained, through faith in Christ, that for which he has been vainly striving. He has the righteousness which the law requires... With the righteousness which is 'through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith' (Philippians 3:9), Paul was sure that he would stand secure in the day of Christ.
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner, the 1888 messenger, on the sinner covered with Christ's righteousness through faith — quoting Phil. 3:9. The law itself witnesses to the genuineness of this imputed righteousness; the believer stands secure not by law-works but by 'the righteousness which is of God by faith.'

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: Men must not only become just by faith—by dependence upon the word of God—but being just, we must live by faith. The just man lives in precisely the same way and by precisely the same thing that he became just.
witnesses.gloss: Jones, the other 1888 messenger, on Hab. 2:4 / Rom. 1:17: the believer becomes just by faith and then lives the whole Christian life by that same faith — righteousness by faith is continuous, not a one-time transaction followed by law-works.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: We become just by faith; faith is entire dependence on the word of God. We, being just, must live by precisely the same thing by which we become just; that is, by entire dependence upon the word of God.
witnesses.gloss: Jones defines the faith that both justifies and sanctifies as entire dependence on the word of God — confirming that the imparted life (Gal. 2:20) flows by the same faith that receives the imputed title.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The point that has been urged upon my mind for years is the imputed righteousness of Christ. I have wondered that this matter was not made the subject of discourses in our churches throughout the land, when the matter has been kept so constantly urged upon me, and I have made it the subject of nearly every discourse and talk that I have given to the people.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the imputed righteousness of Christ as the central, Heaven-urged theme — corroborating that this doctrine (Rom. 4:22-25) is the burden of the message, not a peripheral point.

historyAnchor: The message of justification by faith was proclaimed by E. J. Waggoner and A. T. Jones at the 1888 Minneapolis General Conference and identified by Ellen White as "the third angel's message in verity" (Review and Herald, April 1, 1890 = 1SM 372.2).
uncertainties: The section brief lists Waggoner refcodes GTI (The Glad Tidings), WOR (Waggoner on Romans, esp. Rom. 8:3-4), and EVCO (The Everlasting Covenant) and Jones's CWCP; I verified GTI and CHR and LOF_ATJ resolve in the local corpus but selected the CHR 62.1 and LOF_ATJ 38.8-9 passages as the tightest fit for this section's imputed/imparted-and-live-by-faith thesis. A dedicated WOR passage on Rom. 8:3-4 was not pulled here and could strengthen the imparted-righteousness leg if desired.
The RH April 1, 1890 date for the 'third angel's message in verity' statement is confirmed only via its reprint attribution inside 1SM 372.2; I did not separately open the RH periodical entry itself.

The `bible egw "REF"` lookup errors on refcodes containing a paragraph dot (e.g. 'AA 563.1' or 'LOF_ATJ 9.1') because the FTS parser trips on the '.'; I worked around this by reading the page-level code (e.g. 'AA 563') and confirming the paragraph text there, so every quoted paragraph was read verbatim before citing.
